notes.content: Liberal Studies B.A. Elementary Teaching Content Preparation Program is a pre-professional Subject Matter Preparation waiver program leading to enrollment in a Multiple Subject Credential Program (MSCP or Education Specialist Credential Program (ESCP). Successful completion of the major, with either a 2.67 overall grade point average or a 2.75 grade point average in the last 60 units fulfills all CCTC requirements for Subject Matter Competency. Please see the Chair of the Department of Liberal Studies or the Coordinator of the Credential Program ( Department of Teacher Education ) for specific details. Liberal Studies majors may be admitted to the credential program prior to completing their bachelor degrees. Units in the credential program can be applied as upper-division elective credit toward satisfying the 120-unit requirement for graduation. Currently, admission to the Stanislaus State MSCP requires either a 2.67 overall grade point average or a 2.75 grade point average in the last 60 units. Additional details and information pertaining to entrance into the credential program are available in the College of Education section of this catalog, and at the Department of Teacher Education office. Students should consult with the Credential Services Office for changes in the precise requirements for admission to the credential program. Note : The California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CCTC) is empowered to change credential requirements without prior notice. The University will make changes leading to the credential whenever revisions are required by the CCTC. The AA-T for Elementary Teacher Education is now the recommended pathway for students wishing to transfer to the Liberal Studies Major at Stanislaus State. Courses in the AA-T as well as additional courses listed below fulfill the Elementary Subject Matter Competency (in lieu of the CSET Multiple Subject exam) observing the following: Choosing from options satisfying the standard GE requirements can satisfy most of the Liberal Studies subject requirements. The Liberal Studies Department website provides the appropriate CSUS course selection and a Sample Road Map that combines CCTC requirements with the GE . All courses, excluding labs and unless otherwise noted, require a minimum of 3 semester units or approval of the Liberal Studies Department Chair. Lower-division courses do not fulfill the upper-division major requirements. The California Commission on Teacher Credentialing requires Liberal Studies Majors complete each of the Subject Matter Preparation Program Requirements with a grade of C- or better. The courses that satisfy the CCTC requirement in Early U.S. History and American Government will differ from those community college courses certified for completion of the CSU’s US History/Constitution/American Ideals requirement. See the community college catalogs for approved courses. View information for the Department of Liberal Studies , including Learning Objectives for the department and its programs.

Liberal Studies majors may be admitted to the credential program prior to completing their bachelor degrees. Units in the credential program can be applied as upper-division elective credit toward satisfying the 120-unit requirement for graduation.


Currently, admission to the Stanislaus State MSCP requires either a 2.67 overall grade point average or a 2.75 grade point average in the last 60 units. Additional details and information pertaining to entrance into the credential program are available in the College of Education section of this catalog, and at the Department of Teacher Education office. Students should consult with the Credential Services Office for changes in the precise requirements for admission to the credential program.


Note: The California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CCTC) is empowered to change credential requirements without prior notice. The University will make changes leading to the credential whenever revisions are required by the CCTC.


The AA-T for Elementary Teacher Education is now the recommended pathway for students wishing to transfer to the Liberal Studies Major at Stanislaus State. Courses in the AA-T as well as additional courses listed below fulfill the Elementary Subject Matter Competency (in lieu of the CSET Multiple Subject exam) observing the following:

  1. Choosing from options satisfying the standard GE requirements can satisfy most of the Liberal Studies subject requirements. The Liberal Studies Department website provides the appropriate CSUS course selection and a Sample Road Map that combines CCTC requirements with the GE. All courses, excluding labs and unless otherwise noted, require a minimum of 3 semester units or approval of the Liberal Studies Department Chair.
  2. Lower-division courses do not fulfill the upper-division major requirements.
  3. The California Commission on Teacher Credentialing requires Liberal Studies Majors complete each of the Subject Matter Preparation Program Requirements with a grade of C- or better.
  4. The courses that satisfy the CCTC requirement in Early U.S. History and American Government will differ from those community college courses certified for completion of the CSU’s US History/Constitution/American Ideals requirement. See the community college catalogs for approved courses.

notes.content: The California Commission on Teacher Credentialing requires Liberal Studies majors to complete an approved course in each of the following subjects with a grade of C-, credit, or better. Requirements may be met in GE, in the major, or in additional coursework (courses in the major and concentration must be taken for a letter grade). (Lower Division) Subject Matter Requirements include: Reading, Language, and Literature Oral Communication (Lower Division GE 1C) Composition (Lower Division GE 1A) Critical Thinking (Lower Division GE 1B) Children’s Literature *+ History and Social Sciences American Government (University Baccalaureate Degree Requirement) California History *+ Early U.S. History (Lower Division GE 4A) Ancient World History * Geography *+ Mathematics Foundations I and II Science Chemistry *+† Earth Science (Lower Division GE 5A) Physics *+† Physical Science Laboratory Biological Science (Lower Division GE 5B) Biological Science Laboratory (Lower Division GE 5C) Visual and Performing Arts Art * Music * Theatre * Activity courses (may cross-count with Art, Music, or Theatre subject matter, but must be in two different disciplines.) *These areas can be satisfied at the community college with a lower-division course. However, choosing an upper-division course (course #3000-4999) upon transfer can satisfy university and/or major requirements in addition to subject matter. See areas below for course options. +These areas can be postponed until after transfer †Contact the Liberal Studies Department for course selection. US History/Constitution/American Ideas The courses that satisfy the CCTC requirement in Early U.S. History and American Government may differ from those community college courses certified for completion of the CSU's US History/Constitution/American Ideals requirement. See the community college catalogs for approved courses.
notes.contentHtml:
The California Commission on Teacher Credentialing requires Liberal Studies majors to complete an approved course in each of the following subjects with a grade of C-, credit, or better. Requirements may be met in GE, in the major, or in additional coursework (courses in the major and concentration must be taken for a letter grade).


(Lower Division) Subject Matter Requirements include:

Reading, Language, and Literature

  • Oral Communication (Lower Division GE 1C)
  • Composition (Lower Division GE 1A)
  • Critical Thinking (Lower Division GE 1B)
  • Children’s Literature*+


History and Social Sciences

  • American Government (University Baccalaureate Degree Requirement)
  • California History*+
  • Early U.S. History (Lower Division GE 4A)
  • Ancient World History*
  • Geography*+


Mathematics

  • Foundations I and II


Science

  • Chemistry*+†
  • Earth Science (Lower Division GE 5A)
  • Physics*+†
  • Physical Science Laboratory
  • Biological Science (Lower Division GE 5B)
  • Biological Science Laboratory (Lower Division GE 5C)


Visual and Performing Arts

  • Art*
  • Music*
  • Theatre*
  • Activity courses (may cross-count with Art, Music, or Theatre subject matter, but must be in two different disciplines.)


*These areas can be satisfied at the community college with a lower-division course. However, choosing an upper-division course (course #3000-4999) upon transfer can satisfy university and/or major requirements in addition to subject matter. See areas below for course options.


+These areas can be postponed until after transfer


†Contact the Liberal Studies Department for course selection.


US History/Constitution/American Ideas

The courses that satisfy the CCTC requirement in Early U.S. History and American Government may differ from those community college courses certified for completion of the CSU's US History/Constitution/American Ideals requirement. See the community college catalogs for approved courses.

notes.content: A concentration is required and must be approved by a concentration advisor. At least six units must be upper-division. Concentration courses require letter grades of C- or better. Please see the Liberal Studies B.A. webpage in the Stanislaus State Academic Catalog for the most recent list of approved concentrations. Up to six (6) semester units of introduction to education courses for any one student from community colleges may transfer to the CSU (Title 5, Section 40409 [b] California Code of Regulations.) Lower-division introductory education courses cover introduction to teaching and credential programs, tutoring methods and tutoring in school settings, classroom observations, and analysis of classroom management techniques and teaching effectiveness. See directly below for course options.
